title: The Python SDK's ZCC entitlement methods: what they read and why they cannot write

prose.text: How the API and the Go SDK shape these calls is in [[zcc.api.entitlements-wire]].

prose.label: Writing.
prose.text: {{python-update-empty-body}} {{python-cannot-write}} What the API does with the empty body is open in [[zcc.api.entitlements-wire:empty-update-effect]].

single-object-wrapped.statement: For ZCC responses, the Python SDK wraps a single-object body in a one-item list, so its entitlement getters work whether the API returns one object or a list.
single-object-wrapped.conditions: Restated from the former Python position of the get-response-shape divergence (verifier w2 E1): the SDK accepts either shape and takes no side.

evidence.after: # ZCC can return either a single object or a list of objects

quotes: # ZCC can return either a single object or a list of objects

python-group-entries-stringified.statement: The Python SDK's entitlement models cast each `groupList` and `deviceGroupList` entry (ZDX: `upmGroupList`, `upmDeviceGroupList`) with `str()`, so a group object arrives as its Python string form rather than as fields.

quotes: self.group_list = ZscalerCollection.form_list(config["groupList"] if "groupList" in config else [], str)
config["deviceGroupList"] if "deviceGroupList" in config else [], str
config["upmDeviceGroupList"] if "upmDeviceGroupList" in config else [], str
self.upm_group_list = ZscalerCollection.form_list(config["upmGroupList"] if "upmGroupList" in config else [], str)

python-update-empty-body.statement: The Python SDK's `update_zpa_group_entitlement` and `update_zdx_group_entitlement` take no arguments and send an empty JSON body.

python-cannot-write.statement: So entitlements cannot be changed through the Python SDK's update methods.
python-cannot-write.conditions: Follows from the empty body; the server's response to it is open.
